First, we substitute $u=\sqrt{x}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,⟹\,2\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=\sqrt{x}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $3$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{\sqrt{3}}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{\sqrt{3}}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{\sqrt{3}}^{a}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡u\,{|}_{\sqrt{3}}^{a} \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡a-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})) \\  & =2\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡a-\frac{\pi }{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/28afd0a065525cd225377165c2164a1ecc254b1be8aba60d64324d14430c3be4.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡a-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =2\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
